newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures dip on API, Iraq combination.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures dip on API, Iraq combination.

text.p: IPE oil and gas oil futures sank to new lows during the afternoon session after NYMEX came in and mirrorred London's mood following bearish API data and confirmation that Iraqi crude was flowing in earnest.
January Brent was trading 85 cents lower at $22.44 a barrel at 1709 GMT.
"It's down on a combination of the APIs and Iraq. The stops went off at $22.60," a floor trader said.
Traders said although the Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food deal had been largely priced into the market, it was still causing a few jitters.
Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency said 350,000 barrels per day of crude were expected to be pumped from Iraq to the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan.

Traders said bearish API data -- which showed a one million barrel build in heating oil stocks in the U.S., including a 665,000 million barrel gain in the key East Coast area -- helped accelerate the downtrend in place since the end of last week.
But many players said that a downward correction had been on the cards for both Brent and gas oil following last week's rally.
"Iraq and the APIs are part of the story," said one trader.
"But I think last week's gains were overdone so I'm not surprised to see it coming off a bit."
Gas oil was similarly bearish. December gas oil, which expires on Thursday, was trading $9.75 down at $203.25 a tonne while January gas oil was down $9.50 at $205.25 a tonne.
